worlds.title: Snowy Peaks
worlds.blurb: Hop through snowy paths, cross a frozen lake on ice floes, and climb to the Peak Castle.

chapters.title: Frosty Path
chapters.intro: Welcome to Snowy Peaks! Snowplows are clearing the roads. Wait for a big gap, then hop!

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What is snow made of?
questions.explain: Snow is frozen water: tiny ice crystals that stick together into snowflakes.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: When water gets very cold, it turns into…
questions.explain: Water freezes into ice at 0 degrees Celsius, which is 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.subject: Road Safety
questions.prompt: On snowy days, cars need…
questions.explain: Snow and ice are slippery, so cars take longer to stop. Always wait for cars to stop before you cross.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: What helps you stay warm outside in winter?
choices: A hat, gloves and a coat
questions.explain: Warm clothes trap your body heat. A hat helps a lot!

chapters.title: Icy Lake
chapters.intro: The lake is frozen in big pieces. Hop onto the ice floes to cross the water!

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: When a lake freezes, where does the ice form first?
questions.explain: Ice is lighter than water, so it floats. Lakes freeze from the top down, and fish stay safe in the water underneath.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Where do wild penguins live?
questions.explain: Wild penguins live in the southern half of the world. No penguins live at the North Pole!

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: How many points does a snowflake have?
questions.explain: Snowflakes almost always have six points, because of the way water freezes.

questions.subject: Road Safety
questions.prompt: Why do people put salt or sand on icy sidewalks?
choices: So shoes and tires don't slip
questions.explain: Salt helps melt the ice and sand adds grip, so people and cars slip less.

chapters.title: Peak Castle
chapters.intro: The last climb! Busy roads, icy water and a castle at the very top of the mountain. You can do it!

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Which animal has thick white fur to stay warm in the snow?
questions.explain: Polar bears have thick fur and a layer of fat to keep warm in the Arctic.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Why is it colder at the top of a tall mountain?
choices: The air up high is thinner and holds less heat
The wind is made of ice
questions.explain: High up, the air is thinner and can't hold as much heat. That's why mountain tops can have snow even in summer.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: What do bears do in winter?
choices: Many sleep for a long time in a den
questions.explain: Many bears rest in a den for the winter and live off their fat. It's called hibernation.

worlds.title: Sunny Shores
worlds.blurb: Hop along a sandy beach, ride surfboards across the waves, and reach the lighthouse at Lighthouse Point.

chapters.title: Sandy Path
chapters.intro: Welcome to Sunny Shores! Hop along the sandy path, and watch for beach buggies.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Which animal walks sideways on the beach?
questions.explain: Crabs walk sideways because their legs bend best that way.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Why is the ocean salty?
choices: Rivers carry salt from rocks into the sea
questions.explain: Rain and rivers wash tiny bits of salt out of rocks and carry them to the ocean, where it builds up.

questions.subject: Road Safety
questions.prompt: What should you wear at the beach on a sunny day?
questions.explain: Sunscreen and a hat protect your skin from sunburn.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: You find 3 shells, then 4 more. How many shells?
questions.explain: 3 + 4 = 7 shells.

chapters.title: Tide Pools
chapters.intro: The tide is coming in! Hop onto the surfboards to cross the waves.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What makes the tide go in and out?
questions.explain: The Moon's gravity pulls on the ocean, so the water rises and falls twice a day.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: How many arms does a starfish usually have?
questions.explain: Most sea stars have five arms, and some can even grow an arm back!

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: What is a tide pool?
choices: Sea water left in rocks when the tide goes out
A swimming pool at a hotel
questions.explain: When the tide goes out, water stays in rocky dips, and little sea animals live there.

questions.subject: Kindness
questions.prompt: You see a crab in a tide pool. What's the kind thing to do?
choices: Look gently and leave it there
questions.explain: Tide pool animals need their home. Look gently, then let them be.

chapters.title: Lighthouse Point
chapters.intro: Last stop: Lighthouse Point! Hop all the way to the lighthouse at the end of the beach.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What does a lighthouse do?
choices: Shines a light so ships stay safe
questions.explain: Its bright light warns ships about rocks and shows them where the shore is.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Is a whale a fish?
questions.explain: Whales breathe air and feed their babies milk, so they are mammals.

questions.subject: Words
questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'sand'?
questions.explain: Sand and hand both end with -and.

worlds.title: Jungle Journey
worlds.blurb: Swing through a rainforest full of parrots and monkeys, cross the river on lily pads, and climb to the Temple Top.

chapters.title: Vine Valley
chapters.intro: Welcome to the jungle! Hop along the trail and watch for the safari jeeps.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Which animal swings from tree to tree?
questions.explain: Monkeys use their arms and tails to swing through the trees.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Why are rainforests so green?
choices: It rains a lot and it's warm
questions.explain: Lots of rain and warm sun help plants grow all year.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: What do parrots use to crack nuts?
questions.explain: Parrots have strong, curved beaks that crack hard shells.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: There are 4 parrots and 3 more fly in. How many parrots?
questions.explain: 4 + 3 = 7 parrots.

chapters.title: Hippo River
chapters.intro: A wide river runs through the jungle. Hop across on the lily pads and logs!

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Where do hippos spend most of the day?
questions.explain: Hippos stay in rivers to keep cool, and come out at night to eat grass.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: What does a caterpillar turn into?
questions.explain: A caterpillar makes a chrysalis, then comes out as a butterfly.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What do frogs start life as?
questions.explain: Frogs hatch from eggs as tadpoles that swim, then grow legs.

questions.subject: Kindness
questions.prompt: A friend drops their snack in the river. What could you do?
questions.explain: Sharing is a kind way to help a friend.

chapters.title: Temple Top
chapters.intro: Last climb! Hop all the way to the old stone temple at the top of the jungle.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Which big cat has spots and lives in rainforests?
questions.explain: Jaguars are big spotted cats that live in rainforests and love to swim.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Which layer of the rainforest is the very top?
questions.explain: The emergent layer is made of the tallest trees, poking up above the rest.

questions.subject: Words
questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'tree'?
questions.explain: Tree and bee both end with the -ee sound.

worlds.title: Sky Islands
worlds.blurb: Float up above the jungle to islands in the clouds. Hop across drifting clouds and find the Rainbow Bridge.

chapters.title: Cloud Meadow
chapters.intro: Welcome to the Sky Islands! Hop from cloud to cloud, and watch for the sky buses.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What are clouds made of?
questions.explain: Clouds are made of tiny water drops or ice, floating in the air.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What do we call water falling from clouds?
questions.explain: When cloud drops get big and heavy, they fall as rain.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Which animal can fly?
questions.explain: Birds have wings and hollow bones to help them fly.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: There are 5 clouds and 2 float away. How many are left?
questions.explain: 5 take away 2 is 3.

chapters.title: Windmill Isle
chapters.intro: The wind is strong up here! It turns the windmills and pushes the clouds along.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What makes a windmill turn?
questions.explain: Moving air pushes the windmill's sails around.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Can you see air?
choices: No, but you can feel it move
questions.explain: Air is invisible, but you feel it when the wind blows.

questions.subject: Road Safety
questions.prompt: A bus stops to let kids off. What should you do?
questions.explain: Wait on the sidewalk until the bus leaves so drivers can see you.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: A windmill has 4 sails. How many sails do 2 windmills have?
questions.explain: 4 + 4 = 8 sails.

chapters.title: Rainbow Bridge
chapters.intro: Last island! Cross the clouds to the Rainbow Bridge at the very top of the sky.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: When do we see a rainbow?
questions.explain: Sunlight bends through raindrops and splits into colors.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: How many colors are in a rainbow?
questions.explain: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet: 7 colors.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Which is NOT a kind of weather?
questions.explain: Rain, snow, wind and sunshine are weather. Pancakes are breakfast!

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: You hop 10 clouds, then 5 more. How many clouds?
questions.explain: 10 + 5 = 15 clouds.

worlds.title: Ocean Deep
worlds.blurb: Dive down under the waves! Hop across giant bubbles, wave to sea turtles, and find the Coral Castle.

chapters.title: Kelp Forest
chapters.intro: Welcome under the sea! Hop through the kelp, and watch for the submarines.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Which animal has eight arms?
questions.explain: An octopus has eight arms covered in suckers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: How do fish breathe underwater?
questions.explain: Gills take oxygen out of the water.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: What is a baby whale called?
questions.explain: Baby whales, like baby cows, are called calves.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: There are 6 fish and 3 swim away. How many are left?
questions.explain: 6 take away 3 is 3.

chapters.title: Turtle Reef
chapters.intro: The coral reef is full of color! Hop on the bubbles to cross the deep water.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: What is coral?
questions.explain: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called polyps.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Why is the ocean salty?
choices: Rivers carry salt from rocks into it
questions.explain: Rain and rivers wash tiny bits of salt from rocks into the sea.

questions.subject: Road Safety
questions.prompt: A submarine is a kind of what?
questions.explain: A submarine is a boat that can travel underwater.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: A starfish has 5 arms. How many arms do 2 starfish have?

chapters.title: Coral Castle
chapters.intro: Last dive! The Coral Castle is waiting at the bottom of the sea.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Which is the biggest animal that ever lived?
questions.explain: Blue whales are bigger than any dinosaur!

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What makes waves in the ocean?
questions.explain: Wind blowing over the water makes most waves.

questions.subject: Nature
questions.prompt: Which ocean animal has a shell on its back?
questions.explain: Sea turtles carry their shell everywhere.

questions.subject: Math
questions.prompt: You hop 8 bubbles, then 7 more. How many bubbles?
